explanations: terra: Blood and what has been dedicated to other than God are forbidden foods, a repeated boundary around the section's altar and carcass.

luna: The section’s root ي س ر links its word yusr (ease) with al-maysir (gambling); here Allah intends “الْيُسْرَ” rather than “الْعُسْرَ” in the fasting rule, making ease a divine provision rather than chance gain. | terra: God explicitly desires yusr for people and not usr, identifying the giver and purpose of the ease whose root also names maysir.
terra: The sacrificial offering must reach its appointed place before release from consecration, so the animal has a prescribed destination rather than an erected pagan stone.

luna: The section’s word al-maysir is the subject of this question; the answer says its sin is greater than its benefit, framing the game’s apparent gain as a loss. | terra: The answer about al-maysir acknowledges human benefits but declares its sin greater, supplying the moral judgment on the apparently profitable division described in the section.
terra: The command qumu lillahi qanitin makes standing an act performed devoutly for God, sharply distinguishing sacred posture from attendance at an erected stone.
terra: The resurrection sign raises the bones and then clothes them with flesh, another precise reversal of meat being stripped from bone.
terra: Abraham is told to prepare birds and place a portion on each mountain before they return alive; divided animal portions serve a resurrection sign rather than gain at play.

luna: The section’s root ي س ر links al-maysir to ease; this ayah uses “مَيْسَرَةٍ” for a debtor’s time of ease, a merciful deferral that contrasts with gambling for a share. | terra: A debtor in hardship must be granted time until maysarah; this cognate of the section's y-s-r root makes ease an act of mercy in an economic relation, not the gain of maysir.

luna: This ayah says pens were cast as lots to choose who would care for Maryam; the lot action parallels the section’s arrows, while its own context shows selection for custodianship rather than gambling. | terra: The contenders cast their pens to determine who would care for Mary, a Qur'anic lot scene whose object and context differ sharply from gambling for meat.

luna: The section’s dictionary form al-naṣīb means an appointed share; this verse calls an heir’s portion “نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا,” placing allotment under a prescribed rule rather than arrow-lots. | terra: Inheritance gives both men and women nasiban mafruda, an obligatory appointed share; it is the clearest lawful counterpart to a portion won by arrows.

luna: Continuing the inheritance portions introduced at 4:7, this ayah sets out children’s and parents’ fractional shares as a rule; its own detail shows measured entitlement in place of arrows deciding who receives the camel meat. | terra: God Himself instructs the heirs and fixes measured fractions for children and parents, replacing chance apportionment with an explicit legal division.

luna: This ayah continues the prescribed inheritance shares with fractions for spouses and siblings; its own allocation by kinship extends the contrast with the section’s chance-drawn portions. | terra: The remaining inheritance fractions are likewise fixed by divine instruction, extending the lawful model of an assigned share beyond the summary in 4:7.
terra: The ban on consuming one another's wealth wrongfully, with mutually agreed trade as the stated alternative, locates gambling's transfer of wealth outside legitimate exchange.

luna: The section’s dictionary word al-naṣīb means a share; this ayah gives men and women a “نَصِيبٌ” from what they earn, grounding a person’s portion in accountable earning rather than the section’s chance-drawn stake. | terra: Men and women each have a nasib from what they earn and are told to ask God for His bounty, linking apportioned benefit to effort and divine gift rather than a wager.
terra: The instruction to give covenant partners their nasib presents a named, owed share within an ordered inheritance setting.
terra: God fixes the sibling shares in the final inheritance ruling and says He makes the law clear, another explicit alternative to allocation by chance.

luna: Immediately before 5:3, this ayah forbids violating Allah’s rites and the sacrificial offerings; it establishes protected, God-marked sacrifice before 5:3 distinguishes it from slaughter at the standing stones and allotment by arrows. | terra: Sacrificial animals and their garlands are declared inviolable signs on the way to the Sacred House, supplying a sanctioned ritual-animal setting opposite the ansab.

luna: This ayah forbids both slaughter “عَلَى النُّصُبِ” and seeking shares “بِالْأَزْلَامِ”; it names the altar and arrow-allotment practices that the section reconstructs. | terra: It directly forbids both an animal slaughtered on al-nusub and seeking an allotted division with al-azlam, joining the bloodied stone to the arrows that assign portions.
terra: The two sons of Adam offer sacrifices, but acceptance belongs only to the mindful; ritual killing by itself therefore cannot secure a favorable outcome.

luna: The section’s words al-maysir, al-anṣāb, and al-azlām appear together here as “رِجْسٌ مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ,” giving the camel-and-stone scene its explicit Qur’anic judgment. | terra: This ayah gathers the section's whole scene in one ruling: al-maysir, al-ansab, and al-azlam are filth from Satan's work.

luna: As the next ayah after 5:90, it names al-maysir’s effects: enmity and diversion from Allah’s remembrance and prayer. That consequence opposes the section’s movement toward the Lord. | terra: Following 5:90, this ayah names what gambling produces—enmity and hatred—and how it diverts people from God's remembrance and prayer.

terra: A deliberately killed game animal requires an equivalent livestock offering assessed by two just people and brought to the Kaaba, replacing chance division with measured judgment and a named destination.
terra: The Kaaba, sacred month, sacrificial animals, and garlands are designated supports for people, identifying the divinely ordered center and objects of sacrifice.
terra: The invented categories of consecrated livestock—bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah, and ham—extend the section's pre-Islamic animal-and-cult setting and identify it as a fabrication against God.
terra: Eating is permitted where God's name has been mentioned, supplying the positive ritual boundary for the slaughter scene.
terra: The prohibition on eating what lacks God's name identifies the decisive fault in cultic slaughter independently of how its meat is divided.

luna: The section’s root ش ر ح and word ṣadr recur in “يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ”; the same ayah contrasts that opening with a constricted chest, making the image a sign of guidance and its opposite. | terra: God's guidance is expressed as opening the breast for surrender, while misguidance makes it constricted; the ayah also ends with rijs, the term applied to the gambling-and-altars complex in 5:90.

luna: The section’s dictionary word al-naṣīb means a set share; here “نَصِيبًا” is assigned from crops and livestock to Allah and partners, exposing rival cultic allocations beside the camel-and-stone scene. | terra: The idolaters assign a nasib of crops and livestock to God and another to their partners; this exposes cultic apportionment itself rather than merely the objects worshipped.

terra: Between the livestock shares of 6:136 and the invented restrictions of 6:138, the partners make killing children seem fair and thereby confuse the people's religion; it states the destructive power of the same cultic authority.
terra: Continuing the cultic shares of 6:136, this ayah reports livestock and crops reserved by claim, animals whose use was forbidden, and animals over which God's name was withheld.
terra: The contents of certain animals' wombs are assigned to men, denied to wives, and shared if born dead; it is a precise cultic allocation of animal flesh by invented rules.
terra: The food boundary includes flowing blood and an animal sinfully dedicated to other than God; daman masfuhan sharply answers the section's blood poured over stones.

luna: The speaker declares “إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي” are for Allah, Lord of the worlds; this makes sacrifice and worship answer to God, not the section’s blood-marked stones. | terra: Prayer, sacrifice, life, and death are declared wholly for God, Lord of the worlds, setting the proper recipient of ritual slaughter against the ansab.
terra: The revealed Book is accompanied by the command that there be no constriction in the addressee's breast, supplying the boundary opposite sharh al-sadr.
terra: Those who invent lies against God receive the portion appointed for them in the Book until death overtakes them; a fixed nasib answers their false cult claims.
terra: When asked about spoils, the hearers are told that they belong to God and the Messenger and must repair relations and obey, placing contested goods under revelation rather than a wager.

luna: This ayah assigns a fifth of war spoils to named recipients; the specified fraction and beneficiaries give a concrete case of a portion determined by rule rather than by the section’s arrows. | terra: The fifth of acquired spoils is assigned to named recipients by rule, providing another communal distribution governed by revelation rather than a draw.
terra: Alms are assigned to named recipient groups as an obligation from God, presenting communal goods as a divinely fixed distribution.

terra: The Prophet is forbidden ever to stand in the harmful mosque and told that a mosque founded on mindfulness is worthier for standing, making the place and object of upright worship morally decisive.
terra: Thirst, nasab, and hunger suffered in God's path are credited as righteous action, giving concrete content to exertion directed toward the Lord.
terra: People are challenged for turning God's provision into lawful and forbidden portions without authorization, a boundary against humanly invented rules for food.
terra: After describing what the people worship as inherited cult, God promises to pay them their nasib in full; worship and an undiminished allotted portion meet in the same ayah.
terra: God says that the treasuries of all things are with Him and that He sends each down only in a known measure, locating hidden provision and its portion with God.
terra: Each gate of Hell has a juzun maqsum, an assigned portion; the phrase shows apportionment as a fixed judgment rather than a lucky draw.
terra: The people of the Garden will not be touched by nasab, marking freedom from exhaustion as the final boundary of the present command to exert oneself.
terra: God acknowledges that the Prophet's breast is constricted by hostile speech; 15:98 answers that constriction with praise and prostration to the Lord.
terra: The command to glorify the Lord and prostrate answers the constricted breast in 15:97 and parallels the section's movement from bodily state to directed worship.

luna: The section’s dictionary form al-naṣīb is an appointed share; this ayah describes people assigning a portion of God’s provision to beings they do not know, showing how allotment of provision can serve a rival cult rather than a divinely prescribed share. | terra: They appoint a nasib from God's provision to beings they do not know, directly joining an assigned portion, provided goods, and false worship.
terra: Those worshipped apart from God possess no provision for their worshippers, exposing the futility of seeking a material share through cult objects.
terra: A person who opens his breast to disbelief reverses the opening of the breast granted by God; the shared sharh-sadr construction marks the moral boundary.
terra: This repeated food law again joins blood with an animal dedicated to other than God, confirming that the sacrificial addressee governs the meat's status.
terra: The Lord expands provision for whom He wills and measures it, locating both abundance and restriction in His knowledge rather than fortune.
terra: Dhul-Qarnayn promises the righteous a good reward and an easy word from his command, using ease in the act of assigning a just outcome.

luna: The section’s root ش ر ح appears in Moses’s request “رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي”; his plea for an opened chest before speaking gives another prophetic setting for the chest-opening named in 94:1. | terra: Moses says rabbi ishrah li sadri, bringing Rabb, sharh, and sadr together in a prayer and making the section's three lexical strands meet in one address.
terra: Moses then asks God to make his task easy, wa-yassir li amri; beside 20:25, ease is requested from the Lord rather than obtained from maysir.

luna: Abraham asks his people about “التَّمَاثِيلَ” to which they are devoted; these worshipped images parallel the section’s erected stones and make the object of devotion itself visible. | terra: Abraham asks why his people remain devoted before their statues; their bodily devotion to objects clarifies the section's contrast with turning toward Rabb.

luna: In the pilgrimage passage continued by 22:34 and 22:36, this ayah directs pilgrims to name Allah over the livestock He provided and to eat and feed the poor; its own contribution is a God-directed sharing of sacrificial meat, unlike the section’s arrow-divided camel. | terra: At the appointed days God's name is spoken over provided livestock, after which people eat and feed the destitute; the meat is shared as worship and care rather than gambling.

luna: This ayah in the same pilgrimage passage commands avoidance of the filth of idols; it directly marks the worship of standing stones as the rejected side of the legitimate rites described in 22:34 and 22:36. | terra: The command to avoid rijs min al-awthan gives cult-images the same impurity language that 5:90 applies to maysir, ansab, and azlam.

luna: This ayah says that honoring Allah’s signs is from piety of the hearts; beside 22:36, which calls sacrificial camels Allah’s signs, it distinguishes God-oriented rites from the section’s blood-offering to stones.

luna: This ayah says the sacrificial animals’ destination is the Ancient House; alongside 22:34’s prescribed rite, its own detail gives a sanctuary-directed setting for animal sacrifice rather than the section’s erected altar stones. | terra: Sacrificial animals have benefits until an appointed term, but their proper destination is the Ancient House; the ayah replaces an arbitrary cult-stone with a divinely named place.

luna: This ayah describes a rite in which communities name Allah over the livestock He provides; it sets animal sacrifice directed to Allah against blood poured on worshipped stones. | terra: Every community receives a rite so that God's name may be mentioned over the livestock He provided; provision, slaughter, and devotion are all returned to the one God.
terra: Between the God-named livestock of 22:34 and the camel sacrifice of 22:36, this ayah defines the humble worshippers as patient, prayerful, and generous from God's provision.

luna: For “الْبُدْنَ,” this ayah commands Allah’s name over the standing camels, then eating and feeding from them; it gives the section’s divided camel meat a sacrificial sharing ordered by God rather than arrows. | terra: Sacrificial camels are lined up with God's name pronounced, then their fallen sides yield food for the contented and the needy; this is the lawful counterpart to cutting a camel into chance-assigned shares.

luna: Following the camel rite of 22:36, this ayah says “لَن يَنَالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَاؤُهَا” but that piety reaches Him; it overturns the section’s image of blood presented on a stone. | terra: Neither the sacrificial animals' flesh nor their blood reaches God; only mindfulness reaches Him, directly denying the efficacy imagined in blood poured upon a cult-stone.
terra: Human formation clothes the bones with flesh; this reverses the section's dictionary image of sharh as flesh cut away from bones.
terra: The servants of the Merciful spend the night prostrating and standing for their Lord, a sustained bodily counter-image to devotion before a cult-stone.
terra: Moses says his breast constricts and his tongue does not flow, a negative state answered elsewhere by the prayer ishrah li sadri in 20:25.
terra: The people say they worship idols and remain devoted to them, staging sustained attendance before cult objects rather than devotion to the Lord.
terra: The she-camel has one drinking share and the people another on a known day, a repeated animal-centered apportionment fixed in advance rather than drawn by arrows.
terra: The hearer is told to seek the Hereafter with what God has given while not forgetting his nasib of worldly life, joining divine gift to a bounded personal portion.
terra: The idols worshipped besides God possess no provision, so the hearers are told to seek provision from God and worship Him; this directly counters seeking a share at cult objects.
terra: The inhabitants of the lasting abode praise God because neither toil nor weariness touches them there; nasab belongs to the journey, not its divinely granted end.

luna: Abraham challenges worship of “مَا تَنْحِتُونَ,” what people carve; this parallels the section’s humanly erected and worshipped stones by confronting devotion to a made object. | terra: Abraham asks whether they worship what they carve, making the manufactured material object in the section's erected-stone scene explicit.
terra: God ransoms Abraham's son with a great sacrifice, presenting slaughter as a divinely given release rather than a wager for portions.

luna: Jonah “فَسَاهَمَ” (cast lots) aboard the ship; the same lot-drawing action as the section’s meysir serves here to identify a passenger, not divide a gambling stake. | terra: Jonah participates in a drawing of lots and becomes one of those who lose; the ayah shows a lot selecting a person and an outcome rather than assigning cuts of a carcass.
terra: The night worshipper alternates prostration and standing while fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the Lord's mercy, showing upright exertion directed by knowledge and hope.

luna: The section’s root ش ر ح and word ṣadr recur when Allah opens a person’s chest to Islam; the ayah sets that opening against hearts hardened to God’s remembrance. | terra: The one whose breast God has opened to surrender stands in light from his Lord, repeating sharh and sadr while locating the opening with Rabb.
terra: The seeker of worldly harvest is granted some of it but has no nasib in the Hereafter, showing that the lasting share turns on one's chosen aim rather than chance.
terra: God sends provision in due measure because unrestricted abundance would provoke transgression; the ayah gives a reason for divinely measured shares.
terra: People assign God a portion from His own servants, another idolatrous act of partition that parallels the cultic shares of livestock in 6:136.
terra: Sacrificial animals are described as prevented from reaching their proper place, confirming that lawful offerings have a recognized destination.
terra: The naming of al-Lat and al-Uzza begins the concrete Arabian cult setting whose allocation is condemned as an unjust division in 53:22.
terra: Manat, the third named cult-figure, completes the set immediately before the passage exposes the worshippers' biased apportionment.
terra: The question assigning males to the hearers and females to God states the two sides of the division judged unjust in 53:22.
terra: After the naming of al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat and the assignment of daughters to God, the verdict tilka idhan qismatun diza condemns the cult's unequal division.

terra: The named cult-figures are only names without divine authority, and their followers pursue conjecture and desire; this supplies the epistemic boundary for the arrows and their stones in 53:19-22.
terra: God declares the water qismatun baynahum, an allotted division between the people and the she-camel, giving an animal-centered apportionment fixed by command rather than arrows.
terra: Public wealth is assigned to named recipients so that it does not circulate only among the rich, giving both a rule and an ethical purpose for distribution.
terra: God provides from an unexpected source and has set a measure for everything, directly opposing the attempt to secure one's portion through a random draw.
terra: Whoever is mindful of God is promised yusran in the affair, another explicit case of ease being made by God.

luna: The section’s root ي س ر also names its ease; this ayah promises “بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا” in its directions about spending, echoing ease with hardship and contrasting it with a share drawn by lot. | terra: In the setting of restricted provision and measured spending, God promises to make ease after hardship; the share and the ease are divinely ordered rather than drawn by lot.
terra: The command to leave them plunging and playing until the promised day leads directly into their rush toward a nusub-like goal in 70:43, turning heedless play toward judgment.

luna: The section’s dictionary word al-anṣāb names stones set up for worship; here people rush from graves “كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ,” turning that stone image into an eschatological simile rather than a cultic rite. | terra: The dead rush from their graves as though racing toward a nusub; the simile turns eagerness for the erected cult-stone into an image of resurrection and judgment.
terra: Downcast eyes and enveloping humiliation complete the resurrection rush of 70:43 and disclose the end of their former eagerness toward the erected object.
terra: Qum al-layla commands bodily rising for worship, a close nonlexical parallel to the section's upright exertion after becoming free.
terra: Remembering the Lord's name and devoting oneself wholly to Him states the direction of the exertion that the section contrasts with standing before a stone.
terra: Qum fa-andhir turns rising into a commanded task, while the next ayah identifies the Lord as the one to magnify.
terra: Wa-rabbaka fa-kabbir directs the risen addressee of 74:2 toward his Lord, matching the paired imperatives in 94:7-8.
terra: The person given the record in the right hand receives an easy reckoning, making ease a judged outcome rather than a lucky allotment.

luna: The section’s root ي س ر recurs in Allah’s address to the Prophet, “وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ”; ease is granted for his prophetic course, extending the surah’s promised ease beyond the gambling sense of al-maysir. | terra: The promise wa-nuyassiruka lil-yusra makes ease something God actively prepares for the addressee, matching the section's contrast with chance-drawn fortune.
terra: The faces that are amilatun nasibah—laboring and exhausted—show that exertion by itself can end in fire; direction toward the Lord is what distinguishes the section's fanṣab.
terra: God's messenger identifies the she-camel as God's and protects her drinking share, a compressed parallel to the apportioned camel-and-water scene.
terra: Giving is the first act in the sequence that culminates in being facilitated toward ease at 92:7, opposing the acquisitive logic of gambling.
terra: Affirming the best completes the moral posture that precedes facilitation toward ease in 92:7.

luna: The section’s root ي س ر links ease with al-maysir; after describing giving and God-consciousness, this ayah says “فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ,” an ethically directed ease rather than a chance allotment. | terra: God says fa-sanuyassiruhu lil-yusra, making the easy way the prepared outcome of giving, fear, and truthfulness in 92:5-6.
terra: Stinginess and self-sufficiency begin the contrary sequence completed by facilitation toward hardship in 92:10.
terra: Denying the best supplies the moral cause paired with stinginess before the hard destination named in 92:10.
terra: The miserly denier is facilitated toward al-usra; paired with 92:7, the y-s-r root marks opposed moral destinations rather than luck at the arrows.

luna: The command “فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ” directs prayer and slaughter to “your Lord,” matching the section’s conclusion that upright devotion faces the Lord rather than an altar stone. | terra: The command to pray to your Lord and sacrifice directs both posture and slaughter to Rabb, reversing worship and killing at an erected stone.
